score_rationale.accuracy: Two answer keys reject greetings the lesson itself teaches (q2 accepts only 'Nice to meet you' though 'Hello' is an option; iq9 keys only 'Good morning' though the grammar says 'Hello' works any time), plus small Spanish gaps.
score_rationale.level_fit: Most items are short A1 sentences, but several tutor lines ('I don't think we've met', 'It's getting late. I should go now.') are above A1.
score_rationale.scaffolding: Third-person -s verbs, 'Good evening', 'wife/his' and 'Saturday' are needed for answers but never taught in lessons 01-02.
score_rationale.timing: The amount of content per section fits the two-hour agenda comfortably.
score_rationale.tutor_usability: Two guided practices have confusing role logic or instructions that don't match the dialogue, and some in-class Spanish prompts give the answer away.
score_rationale.relevance_sensitivity: Neighbors, friends, coworkers and class greetings are practical, and nothing asks for disclosure of status, family separation or trauma.

findings.quote: How do you greet someone you are meeting for the first time?
findings.issue: The distractor 'Hello' is also a correct greeting for a first meeting; the lesson's own role-play has the student say 'Hello! Nice to meet you.' and the grammar says Hello works in almost any situation. Auto-graded with no tutor, so a correct learner is marked wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Ask 'What do you say after someone tells you their name for the first time?' and replace 'Hello' with a non-greeting distractor such as 'See you next week'.
findings.verifier_reason: Q2 is an auto-graded single-answer multiple-choice item that accepts only 'Nice to meet you', yet the distractor 'Hello' is also a correct way to greet someone you meet for the first time, as the lesson itself shows (its grammar note says 'Hello' works 'in almost any situation' and its role-play answers a first meeting with 'Hello! Nice to meet you.'), so the key is too narrow.

findings.quote: What do you say at 8 a.m.?
findings.issue: Key is only 'Good morning', but the grammar slide teaches that 'Hello' and 'Hi' work at any time of day, so the key rejects valid answers the lesson teaches.
findings.suggested_fix: Ask 'Which greeting is only for before noon: Good morning or Good afternoon?' or set the key to 'Good morning (Hello / Hi also correct)'.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Listening 2: Introducing a Friend, question 1 (l2q1)
findings.quote: Good evening, everyone! How are you?
findings.issue: The l2q1 answer ('Evening') depends on 'Good evening', which is never taught; the greeting grammar only covers Good morning/Good afternoon 'until evening' and leaves learners with no evening greeting.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Good evening / Buenas noches' to vocab and to the greetings grammar slide, or change the script line to 'Good afternoon' and the question to 'morning or afternoon?'.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Listening 1: A New Neighbor, question 3 (l1q3)
findings.issue: The key needs 'wife' and the possessive 'his', neither taught yet (the script's 'Her name is' is also untaught).
findings.suggested_fix: Key as 'Sofia (his wife)' and tell the tutor to accept 'Sofia', or add 'wife / esposa' to the word list before the listening.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Listening 2: Introducing a Friend, question 3 (l2q3)
findings.issue: The answer depends on 'Saturday'; days of the week are not taught in lessons 01-02.
findings.suggested_fix: Gloss 'Saturday = sábado' on the slide before reading, or ask a question answerable with taught words (e.g. 'Is Marta a student? yes/no').

findings.section: Tutor slides › Guided practice: Introduce the Room
findings.issue: The student must produce third-person -s verbs (teaches; also 'What does he do?'), but lessons 01-02 only teach 'I + base verb'. Third-person -s also appears in role-play lines 'He lives in the next building.' and 'She works with me.'
findings.suggested_fix: Use only 'be' sentences the lesson teaches: 'He is my teacher. He is nice.' / 'She is my teacher.' Or add a short grammar note on he/she + verb-s before this activity.

findings.issue: 'they' and 'we' are glossed only with masculine forms, so learners may think 'they' is only for men; the grammar never says 'they' covers women too. Similarly 'you' is not shown as plural (ustedes).
findings.suggested_fix: Use 'nosotros / nosotras' and 'ellos / ellas', and gloss 'you' as 'tú / usted / ustedes'.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Role-play: Part 1: Meeting a new neighbor
findings.issue: Unnatural Spanish for 'Nice to meet you too'; native speakers say 'Igualmente' or 'El gusto es mío'.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to 'Igualmente.' or 'El gusto es mío.'

findings.section: Tutor slides › Listening 2: Introducing a Friend, question 4 (l2q4)
findings.quote: ¿Cuándo los verá la maestra otra vez?
findings.issue: The English 'Teacher' has no gender, but the Spanish assumes a female teacher, while elsewhere the lesson uses 'maestro'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use '¿Cuándo los verá el/la maestro/a otra vez?' or name the teacher.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Role-play: Part 1: Meeting a new neighbor
findings.quote: Hello! I don't think we've met.
findings.issue: Present perfect contraction is well above A1 for a tutor model line; also in Part 3: 'It's getting late. I should go now.'
findings.suggested_fix: Use 'Hello! I am your new neighbor.' and 'It is late. Goodbye!'

findings.section: Tutor slides › Listening 1: A New Neighbor
findings.issue: Background script uses untaught words (new, apartment, wife, Welcome) that no answer depends on except as noted elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Pre-teach 'new', 'apartment' and 'Welcome' with Spanish glosses on the slide.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Guided practice: Introduce the Room
findings.quote: A new person walks in. Introduce your tutor to them.
findings.issue: The tutor is both the person being introduced and the one asking 'Who is this?', so the role logic is confusing; the model answers also assume a male tutor ('Este es mi maestro', 'What does he do?').
findings.suggested_fix: Have the student introduce a classmate or a photo of a person, and give both forms: 'This is my teacher. He / She is ...'.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Guided practice: Greet Three Ways
findings.quote: Greet your tutor in the morning and ask how they are.
findings.issue: Title promises three ways and the word bank lists Good afternoon and Hi, but the instructions and dialogue cover only one morning greeting; sessions may not be in the morning.
findings.suggested_fix: Instruct: 'Greet your tutor three ways: Good morning, Good afternoon, Hi. Then ask How are you?' and repeat the dialogue with each greeting.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Role-play: Part 2: Introducing a friend
findings.quote: Your neighbor is with you. Introduce a friend using pronouns.
findings.issue: The setup tells the student to introduce a friend, but in the dialogue the tutor does all introducing and the student only replies.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a chunk where the student says 'This is my friend ___. He/She is ...', using the word bank.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Role-play: Part 1: Meeting a new neighbor
findings.issue: Word bank marks 'Ana' as '(tu nombre)', but the next tutor line is hard-coded 'Nice to meet you, Ana!', so tutors may read it verbatim rather than using the student's name.
findings.suggested_fix: Write the lines as 'My name is ___.' and 'Nice to meet you, ___!' with a note to use the student's name or a made-up one.

findings.quote: María es mi hermana. Ella es maestra. (____ is a teacher.)
findings.issue: The Spanish prompt shown to the student contains the pronoun ('Ella'), so the item tests translation, not choosing the pronoun from the name; also in cw2 ('Él es de Perú'). 'sister' is also untaught.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate only the first sentence in promptEs ('María es mi hermana.'), as cw3 and cw4 already do.
